rationale: Switching from oral risperidone to aripiprazole LAI (Abilify Maintena) — typically motivated by adherence concerns and the desire to escape risperidone's high prolactin burden. Aripiprazole LAI requires a mandatory 14-day oral aripiprazole overlap after the first injection. Cross-taper: the oral aripiprazole overlap runs concurrently with risperidone continuation; once the overlap is complete and the depot is therapeutic, risperidone is tapered to zero over 2 weeks. Prolactin will normalise over weeks to months after risperidone is stopped — counsel patients with established hyperprolactinaemia symptoms (amenorrhoea, galactorrhoea, sexual dysfunction) to expect resolution. Akathisia risk from aripiprazole is moderate when coming from risperidone — the D2 receptor density is moderately elevated but not as saturated as with olanzapine or quetiapine. Monitor closely in the first 2–4 weeks post-switch. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Administer Abilify Maintena 400 mg IM (deltoid or gluteal). Start oral aripiprazole 10 mg/day — 14-day oral overlap MANDATORY. Continue risperidone 4 mg. Warn patient about akathisia. Check baseline prolactin if not already documented.

Day 7: Continue oral aripiprazole 10 mg + risperidone 4 mg. Depot reaching therapeutic levels. Assess akathisia. EPS risk: aripiprazole adds moderate EPS on top of risperidone — anticholinergic cover if needed.
STOP oral aripiprazole (14-day overlap complete). Depot now therapeutic. Taper risperidone to 2 mg. Prolactin begins normalising — patients may notice symptom improvement within weeks.
Reduce risperidone to 1 mg. Depot providing full antipsychotic cover. Continue EPS/akathisia monitoring.
Stop risperidone. Second Maintena injection due today (400 mg). Monthly thereafter. Prolactin recheck at 3 months if baseline was elevated.
